title: Filling a Memory Segment
statement: Let a program with limits $L$ have procedure $p$ equal to the specified fill procedure. For any initial memory $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, destination $a\in\mathbb N$, length $n\in\mathbb N$, and value $x\in\mathbb Z$, suppose the word bound is at least the space bound and $a+n\le L.space$. On input $(a,n,x)$, the procedure has an execution taking at most $13n+6$ steps whose final memory contains $n$ consecutive copies of $x$ starting at $a$ and agrees with $\mu$ at every location outside those $n$ positions.
hypotheses_covered: The space bound is at most the word bound
$a+n$ is at most the space bound
